exact_claim: Destroying a current inventory or facility does not end proliferation when technical knowledge, strategic motive, restart capacity, and political grievance remain.
mechanism: Physical interdiction resets material progress while leaving the causes and reconstruction path intact. Repeated coercive intervention can improve concealment and increase the value assigned to a successful breakout.
antecedents: Counterproliferation literature; preventive-strike debates; safeguards history; sanctions and rollback cases.
framework_contribution: Treats restart conditions as a control variable and makes recurrence an explicit program failure rather than an external surprise.
falsification_test: Show a class of cases in which inventory destruction, without incentive change, continuing monitoring, or material control, reliably prevents reconstitution over the relevant strategic horizon.
responsible_actors: Counterproliferation planners; safeguards authorities; sanctions designers; regional security providers
first_action: Red-team the recurrence model against historical cases and publish exceptions.

exact_claim: A nonproliferation regime defeats breakout only when detection, technical attribution, and effective response complete before a violator can convert breakout into coercive advantage.
mechanism: The governing inequality is T_detect + T_attribute + T_respond < T_breakout_to_coercive_advantage. The response may begin with reversible inspection, service, financial, procurement, and defensive measures rather than force.
antecedents: Breakout-time analysis; safeguards timeliness goals; arms-control verification; crisis-response planning.
framework_contribution: Moves the comparison from time-to-material or time-to-bomb to time-to-coercive-advantage, and includes institutional adjudication and response latency.
falsification_test: Demonstrate that a slower detection and response chain still denies coercive advantage across the shortest credible breakout scenario.
responsible_actors: IAEA safeguards; CTBTO/NDCs; national intelligence; technical findings bodies; defense and economic response coalitions
first_action: Build a case-specific latency budget and exercise the full detect-to-reversible-response chain.

exact_claim: Compliance becomes durable only when it supplies a superior package of security, energy reliability, finance, status, scientific access, and institutional continuity than concealed hedging or possession.
antecedents: contractible benefits that are suspended predictably for noncompliance and restored predictably after cure.
framework_contribution: NPT peaceful-use bargain; fuel-assurance mechanisms; alliance assurance; sanctions relief; development finance conditionality.
falsification_test: Integrates these benefits into one participation product and tests them against the functions assigned to nuclear weapons.
responsible_actors: Identify decisive actors for whom the complete compliance package remains materially inferior to nuclear acquisition, then specify the missing service.
first_action: IAEA; World Bank and regional banks; fuel suppliers; insurers; utilities; security guarantors; member governments
canonical_source: Price and stress-test a multi-supplier nuclear-services compact for one participating utility and state.

exact_claim: A state must be able to disclose and reverse a prohibited activity without the disclosure itself becoming a predictable pathway to regime removal.
mechanism: A bounded safe-harbor process freezes activity, preserves evidence, enables managed access and material transfer, converts facilities, protects against opportunistic exploitation, and terminates if deception continues.
antecedents: Voluntary disclosure programs; sanctions settlements; verified dismantlement cases; safeguards corrective action.
framework_contribution: Couples nuclear cure with a security standstill and an objective restoration schedule while preserving consequences for repeated deception.
falsification_test: Show that threatened regimes disclose early at comparable rates when disclosure predictably increases existential vulnerability.
responsible_actors: Participating governments; IAEA; sanctions authorities; security guarantors; rollback secretariat
first_action: Run a confidential tabletop with a state-role red team and test whether disclosure is a rational choice at each inject.

exact_claim: Technical findings must be evidence-based, reproducible, and institutionally separate from the decision to impose political, economic, defensive, or military consequences.
mechanism: Evidence custodians produce provenance-bearing packets; an independent panel grades findings and uncertainty; legally authorized bodies choose consequences. No target state vetoes a finding about itself, and the technical panel does not command force.
antecedents: Safeguards reporting; CTBTO technical analysis; regulatory adjudication; intelligence assessment practice; due-process design.
framework_contribution: Defines a federated evidence interface and a constitutional boundary between fact production and coercive authority.
falsification_test: Show that a unified body can retain scientific credibility, due process, and restraint while also controlling sanctions and force under adversarial political conditions.
responsible_actors: IAEA; CTBTO; national laboratories; intelligence providers; verification institutes; compact parties
first_action: Blind-test the evidence schema on a false positive, a concealed anomaly, compromised telemetry, and denied access.

exact_claim: Every reversible penalty should have objective cure conditions and a scheduled step-down so corrected compliance does not require a fresh grand bargain.
mechanism: The same legal instrument that activates service holds, procurement restrictions, financial measures, or monitoring enhancements specifies the evidence required to unwind them.
antecedents: Sanctions snapback and waiver practice; contractual cure periods; regulatory consent orders.
framework_contribution: Makes restoration as executable as escalation and treats irreversible punishment as a proliferation incentive.
falsification_test: Demonstrate that discretionary, politically renegotiated relief produces equally reliable early disclosure and cure.
responsible_actors: Compact legislatures and executives; finance ministries; suppliers; insurers; rollback secretariat
first_action: Draft one measure from trigger through cure, audit, and automatic reinstatement, then test it legally.

exact_claim: Successor missions and transition finance for arsenal laboratories, production sites, bases, contractors, workers, and host communities must be legally committed before binding reductions concentrate losses.
mechanism: Milestone-based escrow funds verification, cleanup, energy, medical, monitoring, space, resilience, and conventional-defense missions as arsenal work contracts.
antecedents: Defense conversion; base realignment; chemical-weapons facility conversion; just-transition finance.
framework_contribution: Treats domestic arsenal institutions as control-system actors whose incentives can restore or defeat the transition.
falsification_test: Show durable reductions that survive elections and crises despite unfunded concentrated losses in the institutions capable of reconstitution.
responsible_actors: Legislatures; finance ministries; nuclear laboratories; defense ministries; unions; host communities; development banks
first_action: Create a conversion-estate inventory and appropriate protected escrow before negotiating workforce contraction.

exact_claim: Deep reductions are safe only when every actor, alliance relationship, supplier path, and sanctuary capable of resetting the relevant security equilibrium is included or covered by a credible substitute.
mechanism: The framework evaluates strategic systems rather than signature counts. An excluded actor that can recreate the motive for hedging blocks progression at the current gate.
antecedents: Regional security-complex analysis; arms-control participation requirements; alliance assurance.
framework_contribution: Defines coverage functionally and uses it as a stop condition rather than an aspiration.
falsification_test: Show a case in which a decisive excluded actor can reset force planning but covered states nonetheless sustain deep, verified reductions without replacement hedging.
responsible_actors: Nuclear powers; affected allies; regional guarantors; supplier coalitions; treaty parties
first_action: Map one regional equilibrium and name every actor capable of resetting it.

exact_claim: Nuclear knowledge cannot be erased; the attainable end state is one in which material and industrial reconstitution paths are visible, bounded, symmetric, slow, and unable to produce unilateral coercive advantage.
mechanism: Continuing material custody, facility monitoring, procurement visibility, withdrawal-surviving obligations, and collective defensive response turn retained competence into managed latency rather than an operational arsenal.
antecedents: Nuclear latency literature; safeguards; fissile-material control; post-disarmament verification studies.
framework_contribution: Connects latency to a measurable coercive-advantage margin and to a complete service and security replacement system.
falsification_test: Show that knowledge elimination is feasible, or that visible symmetric latency cannot be stabilized even when response remains faster than reconstitution.
responsible_actors: Nuclear powers; IAEA; future warhead verification directorate; material custodians; regional security coalitions
first_action: Run a withdrawal and reconstitution simulation against the shortest credible response margin.

exact_claim: MAD is retired only when operational nuclear forces no longer supply a unique security, alliance, status, energy, or domestic-continuity service that the replacement architecture cannot deliver more reliably.
mechanism: Each nuclear motive is paired with a tested substitute, and the system is held at its current gate whenever a unique function remains.
antecedents: Deterrence mission analysis; assurance studies; disarmament sequencing; institutional transition design.
framework_contribution: Converts abolition from a numerical endpoint into a functional acceptance test.
falsification_test: Identify a residual unique function after all stated gate conditions pass, or show that the test cannot distinguish stable zero from brittle zero.
responsible_actors: National security councils; alliances; legislatures; treaty institutions; independent inspectors general
first_action: Apply the motive-substitution matrix to one nuclear posture and publish the unfilled functions.

exact_claim: The first 1,000 days should qualify decision-time protection, services, rollback, verification, response, security substitution, and conversion before deep dismantlement is treated as a program objective.
mechanism: Four pilots and nineteen gate metrics generate operational receipts under stress, including false positives, supplier loss, denied access, degraded communications, and verification surrogates.
antecedents: Systems qualification; treaty implementation commissions; military exercises; regulatory stress testing.
framework_contribution: Replaces summit-calendar progress with acceptance-test progress and explicit stop conditions.
falsification_test: Show that immediate reductions without qualified replacement systems are equally durable under uncertainty and political turnover.
responsible_actors: Founding governments; program board; technical institutions; utilities; regional security providers; legislatures
first_action: Fund and schedule the four pilots listed in FIRST_1000_DAYS.csv.

short_name: Four operating systems plus a constitutional bargain
exact_claim: The transition should be built as four service-producing operating systems, followed by a constitutional bargain that admits military stockpiles and production estates into common limits, verification, reduction, and managed latency.
mechanism: Risk and notification, compliance dividend, verification and response, and conversion systems can mature under existing or coalition authority. Military declarations, symmetry, ceilings, dismantlement, and withdrawal-surviving obligations require sovereign strategic agreement.
antecedents: Layered arms-control implementation; functional international organizations; regime complexes; phased disarmament proposals.
framework_contribution: Assigns each lever to the smallest authority capable of operating it and prevents universal-consensus dependence from blocking no-regrets construction.
falsification_test: Show that the architecture omits a necessary operating system, assigns an action to an incapable authority, or creates a sequencing dependency that cannot be satisfied.
responsible_actors: National governments; IAEA; CTBTO; HCoC; ABACC; development banks; alliances; nuclear powers; legislatures
first_action: Convene an authority-mapping review and mark each action startable, coalition-dependent, or nuclear-power-dependent.
